analyst_view.overall: Early view: Gil Vicente are 7th and have just won 2-1 at Santa Clara, but they are the league's tightest side in both directions (10 scored, 8 conceded). Estoril are bottom with 2 points from 10 games and only 5 goals; Vasco Matos left in October, Sérgio Raimundo has been in temporary charge and the club has been looking for a permanent coach, so the bench could be different by kick-off. Yanis Begraoui is close to returning from a muscle injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean lower: Gil Vicente's 11 games have produced just 18 goals, and Luís Pinto himself said his side needs to be more ruthless in front of goal. Estoril have scored 5 times in 10 games, so even a home win looks likely to be by a narrow score.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners. Gil Vicente usually sit in a compact block, but at home against the bottom side they should have more of the ball. The two effects roughly balance, so I keep to the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, which looks low. Gil's 0-0 with Vitória was full of fouls, their games this season include Elimbi's red card against Porto, and Estoril, bottom and changing coaches, are desperate for points. I lean higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, which is a lot for these two attacks. Gil's style is patient and Pinto has publicly asked his players to shoot more, which tells you they are not doing so now. Estoril have created little all season.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. With Gil scoring under a goal a game and Estoril barely half a goal a game, I lean lower. Begraoui's return could help Estoril, but he has been out since September.
